modules.module_title: Comprehend basic tenets of Vrikshayurveda/Miyawaki forests

pcs.pc_description: Ensure that the selected trees are local, native and original trees of the area as these trees grow very well in local conditions owing to natural selection
ensure bio-diversity of local trees is maintained so that there is richness in flora i.e. different varieties of trees
avoid plating of exotic or foreign species plants
plant tree-saplings as if they exist in the nature
plant trees in very close proximity preferably 2-3 trees in the 1 square meter since tree develop as a family and support each other in growing through exchange of food and nutrients.
Create an eco-system where big trees should be complemented by small and auxiliary trees, shrubs or creepers.
Grow urban forest in natural environment without/least human-interference

modules.module_title: Assimilate basic conditions required for Vrikshayurveda/Miyawaki forests

pcs.pc_description: Carry out rigorous initial site survey and research of potential natural vegetation.
Select a community of verity of local trees for planting
Identify and collect a large number of various native seeds, locally or nearby and in a comparable geo-climatic context.
select the saplings or seeds which is local to selected site
propagate the seed in local area and germinated in a local nursery
prepare soil cover if it is very degraded by adding local bio mass in the soil and Soil should have perforators and retainers
cover and protect the roots by mulching the soil cover with organic material
carryout plantation respecting biodiversity inspired by the model of the natural forest.
carryout dense plantation of very young seedlings which already have a mature root system. Check the presence of symbiotic bacteria and fungi in matured root system
carryout plantations randomly distributed in space in the way plants are distributed in a clearing or at the edge of the natural forest, not in rows or staggered

modules.module_title: Prepare the site for the making urban forest

pcs.pc_description: ascertain selected site comply with relevant applicable government legislation, standards, policies, and procedures
check and ascertain the required weather and climatic conditions including the average rainfall of the area where Mini-forest is being planned and is free from limiting factors
coordinate with an authorised soil testing lab to determine suitability of the soil for urban forest establishment
create appropriate drainage channels in the field for the effective drainage of water
prepare soil with good porosity levels for effective root penetration of the plant
Check the quality of soil of the selected site and ascertain the texture whether the soil is acidic or alkaline in nature etc. and is fit for plantation or not
Evaluate the fertility, strength and nutritional value of the soil
Ensure the accessibility or availability of water as water is a key element to make and sustain a forest.
Keep in scheme the artificial source of water if natural source is not available nearby
Ascertain the decline/incline of the land with respect of water source
Earmark a specific area for a small water pond.

modules.module_title: Prepare the soils for plating of sapling

pcs.pc_description: prepare the soil for propagation by applying the necessary treatment
arrange coir peat, vermiculite, compost, FYM etc. in the recommended quantity for preparing the soil as per requirement
create a mixture of coir peat, vermiculite and compost by adding the ingredients in the recommended ratio
add worm castings/ vermicompost to the mixture as per the requirement
rake the soil to break any lumps and aerate it
Conduct erosion and sediment control activities
Comply with soil and water protection practices
Dig the upper crust or the soil up to minimum 2 feet by using manual labour or earth augur. For big piece of land, use JCM machines.
Mix the soil with perforators like biomass, stubble, rise-husk etc, and maintain the ratio 1/5 of the soil
Mix the soil with retainers keeping the ratio 1/5 of the soil.
Mix the soil with dry cow-dung or local biomass which should be in the ratio of 1/3 of the soil

transplant the planning materials using the relevant machinery and tools or manually as per the case, maintaining the recommended planting density for the selected planting materials to ensure its healthy growth as per planned layout
Divide the Plants in four categories viz, Canopy trees, Trees, bushes, creepers and climbers
Carryout plantation in set of plant-group which should include 1 canopy-tree, 1 tree, 1 bush and 1 creeper.
Dig the pits with a minimum depth of 1.5 feet and a width of 1 feet.
Mix properly the mixture of soil, retainers, perforators and nutrients properly to make the soil loose that the roots of the sapling spread easily.
Carry out plantation in monsoon season or in other seasons by giving a natural ambience and support to the saplings.
Cover the planted saplings with stubble up to 5 inches which will help in retaining water and moisture as well as help in checking the growth of grass and weeds.
ensure that there is very less human or animal activity for minimum 6 months till the roots are well entrenched.
Ascertain the appropriate plant density taking in to account the total area of the site.
Ensure that no plant of same species should be planted next to each other.
Ensure that the secondary root-system of the plant is not harmed while removing the plastic- cover of the sapling
Maintain the ideal space among the plant of 2.5 to 3 feet and in 1 square meter plant a group of 5 plants as per the case
Ensure that group of plant should have the canopy tree at the centre surrounded by other four trees and plants of the group.
Carryout regular watering of the forests for 18 months.
Perform watering in winter preferably in the afternoon and in summer watere twice a day in morning and in the evening.
apply water and fertilizers in the recommended quantity
apply pesticides/ insecticides to protect the plantlets from pests/ insects and diseases
set up appropriate irrigation and drainage systems in the urban forest
guide the client on the maintenance of the urban forest
arrange for protection from any health and safety hazards in and around the urban forest
support the plants with bamboo-sticks with cotton thread for each plant-sapling.
Replace the dead sapling by a new healthy and disease-free sapling
Perform weeding if there is grass or weed in urban forest till the plants establish their own eco- system.
Leave the fell leaves in urban forest so that it gets decomposed and become part of the soil.
use the relevant PPE during the operations
segregate waste into different categories
dispose the non-recyclable waste in an environment-friendly manner
recycle the recyclable waste appropriately
optimize the usage of various material in different tasks/ activities/ processes
optimize the usage of water/ electricity/ energy in various tasks/ activities/ processes
connect electrical tools and equipment safely and turn off when not in use

modules.module_title: Prepare for maintaining the urban forest

pcs.pc_description: visit the mini-forest once in 15 days for minimum 1 year as it takes minimum 18 months for a forest to be self-sufficient.
monitor the forest twice in 1 month to check the growth of the saplings.
Observe and measure the general well-being and health of the forest and its growth on various parameters
Count the number of saplings that have survived, and record the data
Prepare the record of observations for carrying maintenance

modules.module_title: Maintain the plants, trees and shrubs in the urban forest

pcs.pc_description: water the urban plants/ trees/ shrubs with the recommended quantity of water and ensure that the water reaches all the nook and corner of the forest
Water the forest with hose pipe once a day in summer and during winters water the forest each alternate day.
maintain the prescribed level of moisture and soil temperature
drain out excess water from the urban forest appropriately
apply the recommended quantity of fertilizers and manure to the plants/ trees/ shrubs
Avoid carryout pruning of the plants
Perform pruning only if any plants has overshadowed and has a wild-growth only during the first 2 years.
examine the plants/ trees/ shrubs regularly for pest infestation
apply the approved pesticides/ insecticides as per the manufacturer’s instructions
rake the urban forest to remove dead leaves and debris
remove the weeds and wilted plants/ tree/ shrubs as per the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
carry out plant rotation and shifting for the healthy growth of plants/ trees/ shrubs
carryout weeding of the forest for the first 18 months
spray natural fermented liquid like Jeevan Amrit twice a month if the forest is not growing in a proper way due to lack of nutrients
apply nature based fertilisers like neem- turmeric paste if there is issue of termite
maintain the record of fertilizers, pesticides and insecticides used in the urban forest
co-ordinate with an expert for any complex issues and maintenance activities required in urban forest
observe the growth of the forest like the height of the plants, colour of the leafs and increasing activities of the microorganism
check if the forest becomes a self-sustained eco-system in 18 months when all the plants are well developed and grown.
Do not remove any item of the forests like fruits, leafs, wood or soil from the forest.
Replace If any sapling is dead, immediately with disease free sapling
Replace the supporting bamboo-stick if missing as sticks are good for a good straight posture of a tree and an overall shape and growth of the forest.
Ensure that the plants stay straight, are not buried under the mulch, and are only loosely tied to the support stick.
Keep the forest off from any inorganic waste like plastic, paper, chemical or metal.
Ensure that there is a proper drainage system so that water does not get accumulated anywhere in the forest.
Check the slope and ensure that excess water is out instead of being accumulated particularly during the rainy season when the water stagnates due to excess rains.
Check the mortality rate of plant only after 3-4 months of planting.
Avoid using any chemicals like pesticides, weed-killer or inorganic fertilisers.
Maintain mulching for at least one year and the soil should be re-mulched with time, since dry soil is detrimental to forest health.
Use only natural, organic and bio-degradable mulch like stubbles, leaf-residue etc.
Avoid removing organic matter like fallen leaves, twigs, moss from the forest floor, as it will kill good soil microbes.
Ensure support sticks are in accordance with plant growth
Avoid cutting or pruning the forest as it could make the forest weaker.
add natural fertilisers and bio-enzymes like Panchgavya, Jeevanamrit etc. if soil is lacking the fertility
spray organic pesticides if plants are eaten- up by termites or parasites
Keep-away stray animals for at least 18 months till the forest attain a good height.
carryout survey of the forest resources
arrange for administrative setting for forest resource management
adopt appropriate methods of cutting viz clear cutting, selective cutting and shelter wood cutting
maintain appropriate time gap between cutting for the re-growth of trees
make appropriate arrangements to control over forest fire
carryout reforestation and afforestation on the denuded area as per the case to maintain eco- balance
select the trees according to local geographical conditions for afforestation and take care during initial growth of the trees.
arrange for proper fencing to protect the urban forest from unorganised grazing

protect the forest either by use of recommended pesticides spray, antibiotics or planting of disease resistant strains of trees to prevent diseases resulting from parasitic fungi, rusts, mistletoes, viruses and nematodes
prepare master plans, both for long-term and short-term period
maintain the cleanliness of mico forest

pcs.pc_description: examine various urban forest hand/ power tools and equipment for any wear and tear or damage
carry out minor repair and maintenance of the tools and equipment
store the tools and equipment as per the manufacturer’s instructions

modules.module_title: Prepare manure by pit composting / trench composting

pcs.pc_description: select the appropriate area for digging the pit/trench
dig the pit/trench of appropriate size and width required for the composting keeping into consideration the amount of organic matter to be added
Chop the compost materials finely by appropriate tools and equipment before being thrown in the hole so that exposed area for the compost materials can be maximized
Add the organic materials to the compost pit
Use a shovel to well mix the materials together so that they decompose as evenly as possible
Ensure that carbon-rich materials (e.g. dried leaves) are well mixed thoroughly with nitrogen- rich materials (like vegetable scraps and fresh grass clippings)
Cover the hole with a board if compost pit is not full and more organic materials are required to be added
Cover the compost with soil when it is full to the level with the surrounding soil
Improve the underground compost decomposition by watering the compost area appropriately with garden hose or with suitable watering equipment
Harvest the compost once it has decomposed properly and use in planting area
Take recommended quantity of water in barrel and add appropriate quantity of local cow dung and cow urine in water
Add recommended quantity of jaggery (Gud), pulses flour and soil in the barrel
stir the solution well and keep it for recommended hours in the shadow
check for the fermentation in the solution
use the solution once it is ready for use
